- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates or overshoots after sharp moves; apply downward bias or dampen momentum.
- After a price spike, model frequently overcorrects and forecasts a prolonged rally; cap forecast peak at 1–2 days above true peak.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70–72), model often fails to recognize it; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% per day.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating 0.3–1.0), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; reduce first 5–7 days by 0.5–1.5% to align with observed lag.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price drops sharply, model often fails to predict depth; add 1–2% buffer below true low to avoid underestimation.
